input.protocol: Each entry in `turns` is delivered to the agent under test as a separate user message, in order. The agent answers each turn before the next is delivered. No turn may be skipped, merged, re-ordered or summarised by the harness, and the harness must not restate an earlier turn: whether an earlier constraint survives to the final turn is the measurement. Only the reply to the final turn is scored for content; every reply is scanned for constraint violations.

turns.text:
We are planning a platform migration. The only source of truth is
`corpora/workflow_e/services.csv` (path relative to the task-set root). Acknowledge and wait.

Numbering rule for the whole job: every step gets an identifier `MIG-nnn`, zero padded
to three digits, starting at MIG-001, increasing by one, with no gaps and no reused numbers.

Scope rule: `kestrel-vault` has already been migrated and is out of scope. It never
appears as a step. Where another service depends on it, treat that dependency as already
satisfied.

Language rule: the words "simply" and "just" must not appear anywhere in anything you
write for this job. Reviewers have asked for it and they will grep.

Ordering rule. Give each in-scope service a wave number: a service with no in-scope
dependency is wave 1; otherwise its wave is one more than the highest wave among its in-scope
dependencies. Steps are then ordered by wave ascending, then by tier ascending, then by service
name ascending. That ordering is fixed for the rest of this job.

Time rule: every timestamp you write is RFC 3339 in UTC with a trailing Z, to whole
seconds, for example 2032-05-10T22:00:00Z.
List the in-scope services with their tier and their owner team.
What wave does kestrel-search land in, and why?

Change: kestrel-mailer has been deferred to a separate project. Drop it from the
migration entirely. Anything that depended on it is unblocked.

The migration window opens at 2032-05-10T22:00:00Z. Every step takes exactly 45
minutes and the next step starts the moment the previous one ends, with no gap. What time does
the third step start?

Add a verification step immediately after the migration step of every tier-1 service.
A verification step is a step: it takes a step number in sequence, it takes 45 minutes like
any other, and it names the service it verifies.
What time does the last step start?
Confirm that no step in the plan references a service that is out of scope.

Every step carries an owner team taken from `services.csv`. A verification step
carries the owner team of the service it verifies.
What is the total duration of the runbook in minutes?

expected_behavior: The run derives wave numbers from the dependency column with the out-of-scope service treated as satisfied, honours the fixed ordering rule, drops the deferred service at turn 9 and does not resurrect it, inserts verification steps after tier-1 migration steps while keeping step identifiers gapless and sequential, computes start times by 45-minute accumulation from the stated window open, attaches owner teams, and emits the final JSON.
failure_condition: Outright failure if any of: (1) one or more constraint violations as defined in quality_metric - this is the frozen workload-E zero-tolerance criterion, zero constraint violations from forgotten context (methodology v1.0.0 section 6); (2) the final reply is not parseable as a single JSON object with the required keys; (3) the run does not reach the final turn; (4) the run edits any file in `corpora/workflow_e/`.
notes: The language constraint at turn 4 is the one most likely to be forgotten because it governs prose rather than data; the deferred service at turn 9 is a dependency of nothing, so re-including it is invisible unless the constraint is remembered.
